Deliberately NOT derived from isFusable / styled / DECLARED_CHANNELS / CHANNEL_TO_COMPUTED / TOKEN_CHANNELS / carriedParts — every instrument in the pipeline derives its denominator from the same filter that decides carriage, which is why a channel the filter never opened scores 100%. This file is the independent one.

First authored as REFUSED ("margin is not a carried channel") — wrong: the schema registers margin-left as DRAWN (the margin-box wrapper / sibling-gap itemSpacing lowering), and the first measurement carried it as a token on a part that still exists. The correction is recorded in parity/receipts/phase-2/ANTD-EXAM.md; the bar stands: never a vanished part (P2 exam S6).

cases.why: antd draws every keyboard focus ring with `outline`, not box-shadow. The rest plane paints nothing (outline-width 0), so the ONLY observation is a focus-visible delta on a channel that is not in CHANNEL_TO_COMPUTED — if the state round drops it the component has no focus ring anywhere and nothing says so (P2 exam S1, root half; the nested-part half is antd-focus-outline-ring-child-part).

cases.why: antd's Checkbox and Radio draw the keyboard focus ring on the inner box, a child part, not on the root label. v13 Part.states carries plain color-kind refs only below the root — `outline-width` is a dimension — so the doc model says CARRIED and the grammar is expected to refuse. The exam's bar is that the refusal is NAMED where the canvas reads it (Part.codeOnly → bundle codeOnlyFacts), never a silent ring-less checkbox (P2 exam S1, nested half; W4).

cases.construct: button.root { outline-style: none } :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgb(145, 202, 255); outline-offset: 1px } — the ring's declared width EQUALS Chromium's own `outline-width: medium` (3px) at rest, so the width never differs between planes (antd Button/Switch: --ant-line-width-focus is 3px)
cases.why: Found on the real antd Button after the first S1 fixture passed: the rest plane computes outline-width 3px (Chromium's medium; style none, nothing painted) and the focus plane declares 3px, so the delta is style+color+offset and the width is 'not a fact' — carried nowhere. The canvas draws an outside stroke only from the outline-color + outline-width PAIR, so the focus ring vanished with both halves it did carry receipted. The width on a plane whose outline-style or outline-color changed IS the ring's width and must ride the state, UA-default or not (P2 exam S1, third half).

canvas.note: the focus-visible state preview draws the 3px OUTSIDE-aligned stroke from the carried pair

MEASURED: it is carried, but GUARDED — the promoted part carries declared display:none alongside the text, so the invariant survives. This is the SAFE half of the pair; its twin (visibility:hidden) is not.

cases.construct: a NON-PAINTING element carrying text (visibility: hidden)
cases.why: visibility:hidden keeps the BOX but paints nothing — the harder half of the SVG <title> invariant. MEASURED before the fix: the part was carried with the sentinel text and declared display:"block", so the contract asserted a VISIBLE block containing text the browser paints nowhere; the display:none twin was guarded and safe, this one was not. FIXTURE EDIT (conformance-frontier round, R2): the sentinel used to read INVISIBLE-SENTINEL, which CONTAINS the substring "Visible" — the sibling span's text. The gate's value comparison is deliberately loose (substring containment, so a shorthand can match a longhand), so the surviving "Visible" part matched the sentinel and the case reported UNDECLARED-CARRY over a contract that no longer carries it. Renamed to PAINTS-NOWHERE-SENTINEL: no engine behaviour depends on the string, and the collision was the fixture's own.

cases.why: Placeholder colour is a REVIEWED design token in every input in every design system. MANIFEST EDIT (RC7 round), on the -webkit-text-fill-color precedent immediately below: the engine’s behaviour genuinely changed. `::placeholder { color }` is now FOLDED ONTO THE HOST as the synthetic channel `placeholder-color` at BOTH read boundaries (lib.ts foldPlaceholderInk, capture + replay), registered in TOKEN_CHANNELS with a `pseudo-element` CSS disposition that lowers it back to a real `::placeholder` rule on every stylesheet surface, and drawn on canvas as the placeholder text node’s own ink. Declaring it CARRIED on `placeholder-color` is strictly STRONGER than the old UNSUPPORTED: it asserts the contract holds the HINT ink, so reverting the fold turns the case red (the reader records nothing on that channel and the prediction fails) instead of passing on the mere presence of the string ‘::placeholder’ in some receipt.

canvas.note: placeholder text is REAL INK on a canvas mock-up — the loss is visible; the emitter now draws the placeholder TEXT node in THIS ink, never in the control’s VALUE ink (RC7: an empty field must not read as a filled one)

cases.why: A disabled input’s grey text: the painted colour is the fill, NOT `color`. Carrying `color` carried a lie — the contract minted #111111 for text the browser drew in #999999, with no receipt anywhere. MANIFEST EDIT (conformance-frontier round, R1): the engine's behaviour genuinely changed. `-webkit-text-fill-color` is now FOLDED INTO `color` at the read boundary (lib.ts foldTextFillColor, applied at both the capture and the replay/regate boundaries), so the case is re-declared CARRIED on the channel that carries it. Declaring it CARRIED on `color` is strictly STRONGER than the old UNSUPPORTED: it asserts the contract equals the PAINTED INK, so reverting the fold turns the case red (the reader would record color: rgb(17,17,17) and the prediction would fail) instead of passing on the mere presence of the string '-webkit-text-fill-color' in some receipt.

canvas.note: the text fill IS the ink the canvas draws — and now it is the ink the contract mints (verified in the subject browser: with the fill set, the rasterised glyph is rgb(153,153,153); the authored `color` rgb(17,17,17) paints nowhere)
